questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. She participates in several functions and musical shows and receives accolades for her singing.

B. Vineeta has a very sweet voice which has inspired her to adopt singing as her profession.

C. She can also play musical instruments such as the sitar and the harmonium.

D. Now, she has opened a music school to train young singers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e. "BACD." 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the abovementioned paragraph, there is a chronological sequence of the sentences.
 
• Sentence B is the first sentence as it begins with the noun 'Vineeta,' and she is the main subject of the paragraph. This sentence establishes her passion for singing, which is crucial to understanding the rest of the paragraph.
 
• Sentence A is the second sentence as it begins with the pronoun 'She' and mentions Vineeta's recognition as a singer. It also implies that she is a talented singer who is appreciated by others. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
 
• The only option that shows such an arrangement is Option 2.
 
• Sentence C is the third sentence as it begins with the pronoun 'She' and provides additional information about Vineeta's musical abilities by mentioning that she can play musical instruments such as the sitar and the harmonium. This sentence adds to Vineeta's characterization as a talented musician and reinforces her passion for music.
 
• Sentence D is the last sentence as it concludes the paragraph by mentioning that Vineeta has opened a music school to train young singers. This sentence ties all the previous sentences together and shows how Vineeta has turned her passion for singing into a profession and a means to help others.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

The correct order is:__ 

B. Vineeta has a very sweet voice which has inspired her to adopt singing as her profession.

A. She participates in several functions and musical shows and receives accolades for her singing.

C. She can also play musical instruments such as the sitar and the harmonium.

D. Now, she has opened a music school to train young singers.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Uma told Susan to give up smoking.

options.text: Susan was told to give up smoking by Uma.
Susan is told to give up smoking by Uma.
Susan has been told to give up smoking by Uma.
Susan had been told to give up smoking by Uma.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e**.**** 'Susan was told to give up smoking by Uma.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice**. We have to change the sentence into **passive form.** 
 
• The given sentence is written in 'simple past tense.'
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• Active Voice: Subject + V2 + Object.
 
• Passive Voice: Object + was/were + V3 + by (preposition) + Subject.
 
 
 
• Let’s see another example:
 
 
• Active voice: I bought a pen.
 
• Passive voice: A pen was bought by me.
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'Uma' and the object of the given sentence is 'Susan'. 
 
• So, in the passive voice, the position of ‘subject’ and ‘object’ will be interchanged. 
 
• Also here, 'told' will be changed into 'was told'.
 
• Here **'to give up smoking'​ **will remain the same.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *Susan was told to give up smoking by Uma.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Renu said to her brother, “You were watching the show without me.”

options.text: Renu told her brother that he had been watching the show without her.
Renu told her brother that he has been watching the show without her.
Renu told her brother that he had watched the show without her.
Renu told her brother that he were watching the show without her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. 'Renu told her brother that he had been watching the show without her.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Direct Speech**. As per the given directions, we have to change it into **Indirect Speech.**
 
• The given sentence is an **assertive** **sentence**.
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
• The conjunction 'that' will be added and comma and inverted commas will be removed.
 
• In the Indirect speech 'said to' will be changed into 'told' because the reporting verb has an object, 'her brother.'
 
• The indirect speech will begin like 'Renu told her brother that.'
 
• Now we have to change the reported speech.
 
• Here the pronoun 'you' will be changed into 'he' and 'me' will be changed into 'her.'
 
• The past continuous 'were watching' will be changed into the past perfect continuous 'had been watching.'
 
• Finally, the indirect speech is 'Renu told her brother that he had been watching the show without her.'
 
• ​So, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *Renu told her brother that he had been watching the show without her.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The audience has being / angry as the magician / is not performing / as expected.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 3) i.e. **'The audience has being.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **'The audience has being.'**
 
• The given sentence is in** passive form** and in **present perfect tense.**
 
• In such cases, we have to use** 'has/have been'** as the helping verb.
 
• The word** 'being'** is incorrect because it is the present progressive form of the verb **'be'**, which should not be used in this context.
 
• Instead, the past participle form of the verb **'be' **should be used, which is **'been'.**
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'has been' in place of 'has being' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct sentence:__* **__**The audience has been**__ angry as the magician is not performing as expected.*

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

Medieval people undertook

P. purify themselves of sin, to transform

Q. pilgrimages individually, travelling to

R. themselves through a trial of faith.

S. distant shrines as a penance to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. "QSPR." 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• In the abovementioned paragraph, there is a chronological sequence of the sentences.
 
• Sentence Q is the first part as the sentence begins with the 'Medieval people undertook' and establishes the context for the sentence by explaining that Medieval people would undertake pilgrimages individually, rather than as part of a group. This suggests that the pilgrimages were a personal, individual experience.
 
• Sentence S is the second part as it answers the next question where and why did medieval people used to go on a pilgrimage? It states that people would travel to distant shrines as a penance to purify themselves of sin. This implies that the pilgrimages were seen as a way to atone for one's sins and seek forgiveness. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
 
• The only option that shows such an arrangement is Option 4.
 
• Sentence P is the third part as it further expands on the purpose of the pilgrimages. It explains that the goal of going on a pilgrimage was to transform oneself through a trial of faith. This suggests that the pilgrimages were not just about seeking forgiveness, but also about personal growth and spiritual transformation.
 
• Sentence R is the last part as it concludes that going on a pilgrimage was a way for people to undertake a trial of faith and transform themselves. This ties together the different parts of the sentence and provides a clear conclusion.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

The correct order is:__ 

Medieval people undertook

**Q.** pilgrimages individually, travelling to

**S.** distant shrines as a penance to

**P.** purify themselves of sin, to transform

**R.** themselves through a trial of faith.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P. Honey ants are common in deserts and other arid climates around the world.

Q. They are part of the “worker” caste of honey ants.

R. Other castes include soldiers, who protect the colony from predators and the queen — usually is the mother of all other ants in the colony.

S. Only some honey ants become “living larders”.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. "PSQR." 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• In the abovementioned paragraph, there is a chronological sequence of the sentences.
 
• Sentence P is the first sentence as it begins with the noun 'Honey ants.' It introduces the subject of honey ants and their prevalence in arid climates around the world. This sentence sets the context for the rest of the paragraph.
 
• Sentence S is the second sentence as it provides specific information about honey ants. It explains that only some honey ants become "living larders," which is some of them store food in their abdomens. This sentence adds more detail to the topic introduced in the first sentence and establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
 
• The only option that shows such an arrangement is Option 3.
 
• Sentence Q is the third sentence as it begins with the pronoun 'They' and mentions that the honey ants that become "living larders" are part of the "worker" caste. This sentence adds more depth to the information provided in the previous sentence and makes the connection between the "living larders" and the honey ants clear.
 
• Sentence R is the last sentence as it concludes the paragraph by providing additional information about the castes of honey ants. It explains that other castes include soldiers, who protect the colony from predators, and the queen, who is usually the mother of all other ants in the colony.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

The correct order is:__ 

**P.** Honey ants are common in deserts and other arid climates around the world.

**S.** Only some honey ants become “living larders”.

**Q.** They are part of the “worker” caste of honey ants.

**R.** Other castes include soldiers, who protect the colony from predators and the queen — usually is the mother of all other ants in the colony.

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.**

The meeting was held upon / for an hour / due to non - availability / of the committee members.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **option 4) i.e. 'The meeting was held upon.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **'The meeting was held upon.'**
 
• According to the rules of preposition, combining two prepositions can lead to redundancy or an awkward sentence structure.
 
• In the given sentence, the prepostions **'upon'** and **'for'** are placed one after another.
 
• Here the prepsition **'upon' **is redundant.
 
• Use of** 'upon'**- used to mean "on" or "immediately after". It is similar in meaning to "on top of" or "upon the surface of".
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• *The decision was made **upon **careful consideration of all the evidence.*
 
 
 
• Use of **'for'**- to denote intention to give; purpose; the result of something; show an amount of time or distance.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• *He was reading the book **for **an hour.*
 
 
 
• The more appropriate preposition in this context would be **"for," **which would indicate an amount of time.
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to remove the preposition 'upon' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct sentence:__* **The meeting was held __**for**__ an hour due to non- availability of the committee members.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Before she came all the work had been completed by me.

options.text: I will complete all the work before she came.
I had completed all the work before she came.
I completed all the work before she came.
I complete all the work before she came.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. 'I had completed all the work before she came.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the** passive voice**. We have to change the sentence into the **active form**. 
 
• The given sentence is written in **'past perfect tense'** form. 
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• Passive Voice: **Object + had + been + V3 + by + Subject**
 
• Active Voice:** Subject + had + V3 + Object.**
 
 
 
• Let’s see another example:
 
 
• Passive voice: **The icecream had been eaten by Rohan.**
 
• Active voice:** Rohan had eaten the icecream.**
 
 
 
• The object of the given sentence is** 'all the work'** and the subject of the given sentence is** 'me.'**
 
• So, in the active voice, the position of ‘**object**’ and ‘**subject**’ will be interchanged and 'by' will be removed. 
 
• **'me' **will be changed into** 'I.'**
 
• Also here,** 'had been completed' **will be changed into** 'had completed.'**
 
• **'before she came' **will remain the same.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:**__ *I had completed all the work before she came.*
